name: stri_datetime_fields
title: Get Values for Date and Time Fields

origin.description: Computes and returns values for all date and time fields.

arguments.name: time
arguments.text: A POSIXct, or a character, Date, POSIXlt, or factor value coerced with as.POSIXct.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: The tzone attribute when omitted. NULL or "" uses the default time zone.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects a calendar.

origin.details: Fourteen fields: Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Millisecond, WeekOfYear, WeekOfMonth, DayOfYear, DayOfWeek, Hour12, AmPm, and Era. Month, AmPm, and Era start at 1. DayOfWeek 1 is Sunday. Week fields follow the locale. A missing instant has missing fields.
origin.value: A data frame with one row per instant.
origin.example:
f <- stri_datetime_fields(stri_datetime_create(2015, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, tz = "UTC"), tz = "UTC", locale = "en_US")
cat(paste0("stri_datetime_fields of 2015-12-31 23:59:59 UTC has Year ", f$Year, " and Month ", f$Month, ".\n"))

arguments.name: time
arguments.text: Seconds since the epoch, a date-time string, NA, or a list of one kind.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: None or "" for the default ICU zone, or one zone identifier. A tzone attribute is not read.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects a calendar.

translation.details: The fourteen columns match stringi. Month, AmPm, and Era are the ICU values plus one. Hour12 is 0 through 11. Pass tz explicitly. The seconds value does not carry an R tzone attribute.
translation.value: A dict of ints when time is a scalar. A list of times returns a dict of lists. NA stays NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.datetime import stri_datetime_create, stri_datetime_fields
f = stri_datetime_fields(stri_datetime_create(2015, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, tz="UTC"), tz="UTC", locale="en_US")
print(f"stri_datetime_fields of 2015-12-31 23:59:59 UTC has Year {f['Year']} and Month {f['Month']}.")
